power

Calculate power for a fixed-size onemean t test

Stata 

power onemean 0 0.5, sd(1) n(40)

R stats 

stats::power.t.test(n=40,delta=0.5,sd=1,type="one.sample",sig.level=0.05, strict = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Noncentral t power counts both tails for two-sided tests. R n is observations/pairs for one-sample/paired tests and per group for two samples; round required n upward.

Stata reference · R reference

Plan the sample size for a onemean t test

Stata 

power onemean 0 0.5, sd(1) power(0.8)

R stats 

stats::power.t.test(delta=0.5,sd=1,type="one.sample",sig.level=0.05,power=0.8, strict = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Noncentral t power counts both tails for two-sided tests. R n is observations/pairs for one-sample/paired tests and per group for two samples; round required n upward.

Stata reference · R reference

power onemean 0, sd(1) n(40) power(0.8)

Differs from Stata Noncentral t power counts both tails for two-sided tests. R n is observations/pairs for one-sample/paired tests and per group for two samples; round required n upward.

21 more examples and alternatives

Calculate correlation-test power at fixed n

Stata 

power onecorrelation 0 0.3, n(100)

R pwr 

pwr::pwr.r.test(r=0.3,n=100,sig.level=0.05)

Differs from Stata pwr uses its documented approximation and effect-size parameterization; numerical results need not equal Stata.

Calculate power for an overall three-predictor R squared test

Stata 

power rsquared 0.1, n(100) ntested(3)

R pwr 

pwr::pwr.f2.test(u=3,v=96,f2=0.1/(1-0.1))

Differs from Stata f2=(R2_full-R2_reduced)/(1-R2_full); residual df is N minus all predictors minus one.

Stata reference · R reference

Plan total n for an overall R squared test

Stata 

power rsquared 0.1, power(0.8) ntested(3)

R pwr 

{ design <- pwr::pwr.f2.test(u=3,f2=0.1/(1-0.1),power=0.8); ceiling(design$v+3+1) }

Differs from Stata f2=(R2_full-R2_reduced)/(1-R2_full); residual df is N minus all predictors minus one.

Stata reference · R reference

Calculate power for incremental explained variance

Stata 

power rsquared 0.2 0.3, n(120) ntested(2) ncontrol(3)

R stats 

stats::pf(stats::qf(0.95, df1 = 2, df2 = 114), df1 = 2, df2 = 114, ncp = 120 * (0.3 - 0.2) / (1 - 0.3), lower.tail = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Two tested and three control predictors: residual df = 120 - 2 - 3 - 1; noncentrality = 120 * (0.3 - 0.2) / (1 - 0.3).

Calculate power for a fixed-size twomeans t test

Stata 

power twomeans 0 0.5, sd(1) n(80)

R stats 

stats::power.t.test(n=40.0,delta=0.5,sd=1,type="two.sample",sig.level=0.05, strict = TRUE)

Stata reference · R reference

Calculate power with unequal independent group sizes

Stata 

power twomeans 0 0.5, sd(1) n1(30) n2(50)

R pwr 

pwr::pwr.t2n.test(n1=30,n2=50,d=0.5,sig.level=0.05)

Differs from Stata Uses the pooled-variance standardized mean-difference model; this is not a Welch heteroskedastic design.

Calculate power for two fixed-size proportion samples

R stats
